facts.title: Oceania — sovereign-country count
facts.text: The source groups 14 sovereign states in Oceania; the count is retained as a geography reference with source attribution.

facts.title: Great Barrier Reef — Queensland scope
facts.text: The Great Barrier Reef is off the coast of Queensland, Australia.

facts.title: Uluru/Ayers Rock — Australia
facts.text: Uluru, also known as Ayers Rock, is in Australia.

facts.title: Canberra — Australian capital
facts.text: Canberra is Australia’s capital; the scan’s Sydney-capital misconception is explicitly corrected.

facts.title: Sydney — Australian city context
facts.text: Sydney is Australia’s largest city by population in common geographic reference usage; this is not a capital claim.

facts.title: New Zealand women’s suffrage — 1893
facts.text: New Zealand’s Electoral Act 1893 established women’s right to vote in parliamentary elections.

facts.title: Great Barrier Reef — ocean
facts.text: The Great Barrier Reef lies in the Coral Sea, part of the Pacific Ocean.

facts.title: Horn of Africa — definition scope
facts.text: A common definition of the Horn of Africa includes Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Somalia; definitions can vary.

facts.title: Horn of Africa — location
facts.text: The Horn of Africa is the easternmost extension of the African continent.

facts.title: Seven Sisters — Indian state group
facts.text: India’s Seven Sisters are Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Tripura.

facts.title: Nordic countries — conventional list
facts.text: The conventional Nordic-country list comprises Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden.

facts.title: Indochina — conventional core
facts.text: Laos, Cambodia, and Vietnam are commonly grouped as the core countries of Indochina.

facts.title: Czechoslovakia — 1993 split
facts.text: Czechoslovakia split peacefully into the Czech Republic and Slovakia on 1 January 1993.

facts.title: Yugoslavia — 1992 dissolution context
facts.text: By January 1992, the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia had ceased to exist; successor-state material is historically scoped.

facts.title: Soviet Union — 1991 dissolution
facts.text: The Soviet Union dissolved in late 1991, producing 15 independent states.

notes.title: Australia terminology and current-office boundary
notes.text: The scan’s outdated Indigenous label and its current-monarchy wording are not stored as unqualified teaching facts. Place names and institutional material are retained only with respectful, date-aware wording.

notes.title: Printed-MCQ quality gate
notes.text: Only the two questions with readable four-option sets, visible printed keys, safe historic/geographic premises, and corroboration are retained. Carbon-tax, monarchy, WikiLeaks, and culturally compressed candidates are withheld.

notes.title: Horn and island-state scope boundary
notes.text: Horn-of-Africa membership varies by definition. The source’s island-state count and broad ocean claims are not imported unless exact geographic scope is independently established.

notes.title: Regional-label boundary
notes.text: Seven Sisters, Nordic, and Indochina are useful regional labels but may vary by geographic, historical, or political convention; retained lists are explicitly scoped.

notes.title: Former-state source-error boundary
notes.text: The scan’s claim that 12 successor states of the Soviet Union were British colonies is rejected as an unsupported source error. Dissolution records are retained only as dated historical material.
